findings.claim: The lifecycle route executor makes its OWN authorization decision by self-constructing a DelegationProof and never consumes a canonical GrantBundle from authority_engine::authorize_execution. lifecycle_executor does not even depend on authority_engine (absent from its Cargo.toml). adapter.rs::execute_route calls authorization::authorize_before_dispatch (authorization.rs:39), which in build_and_write_proof (authorization.rs:57-151) validates a route-supplied delegation_contract and a caller-supplied request.policy.invocation_authority map, then writes its own DelegationProof (struct at authorization.rs:16-37, self-constructed invocation_authority BTreeMap at 85-96). This is a second, self-attesting authority plane competing with authorize_execution.
findings.consequence: There are two divergent sources of execution authority. Agent-route dispatch (the path that spawns Claude/Codex) is authorized by a proof the executor writes about itself from caller-supplied invocation_authority, not by the canonical authority_engine grant. A caller controlling the LifecycleRouteExecutionRequest (route.delegation_contract + policy.invocation_authority) can satisfy the executor's own gate without any authority_engine ALLOW decision, defeating FD-003's single-source guarantee for the highest-consequence effect (process creation of an autonomous agent).
findings.minimum_repair: Make lifecycle route dispatch consume a canonical grant: have the kernel lifecycle driver call authority_engine::authorize_execution for the route and pass the resulting GrantBundle (or a verified ExecutorLaunch token) into the adapter; have authorize_before_dispatch verify that canonical grant instead of (or in addition to) building its own DelegationProof from caller-supplied invocation_authority.
findings.acceptance_test: Construct a LifecycleRouteExecutionRequest with a valid delegation_contract and invocation_authority.mode='unattended' but with NO corresponding authority_engine grant/ExecutorLaunch token on disk; assert execute_route refuses to spawn (returns authorization-proof-failed) rather than proceeding to run_with_timeout/spawn.

findings.claim: No exact one-shot invocation guard is consumed immediately before agent/child-agent process creation. The real Claude/Codex spawn happens at codex.rs:254 (command.spawn()) inside run_with_timeout, reached via execute_agent (codex.rs:76) -> execute_real (adapter.rs:382-407). execute_agent contains no call to verify_authorized_effect, issue_executor_launch_effect, or any grant consumption (confirmed by grep of the whole crate: only string literal reference exists). The kernel driver that reaches this spawn (lifecycle_driver.rs execute_route at line 116; lifecycle.rs; lifecycle_program.rs) contains ZERO references to authorize_execution / verify_authorized_effect / issue_executor_launch_effect / ExecutorLaunch / VerifiedEffect. The one-shot ExecutorLaunch token (single_use=true, issue_executor_launch_effect effects.rs:165-171; consumption marks record.status='consumed' at effects.rs:564-574,649-658) is issued+verified at exactly ONE non-test site: kernel/src/commands/mod.rs:735-745, which gates the 'octon studio' cargo process (action_type 'launch_executor', commands/mod.rs:688), NOT an AI agent. Even the pipeline agent spawn (pipeline.rs:1856 run_with_stdin) is not immediately preceded by an issued+verified ExecutorLaunch token; build_executor_command (policy.rs:36) merely constructs a Command from a profile.
findings.consequence: FD-004's core obligation (every agent AND child-agent launch consumes an exact one-shot invocation guard immediately before process creation) is unmet for the actual agent-execution paths. Process creation of autonomous Claude/Codex agents occurs with no reservation, no single-use consumption, no expiry/revocation check bound to the launch event itself. A replayed or duplicated dispatch can spawn agents repeatedly; a revoked grant does not stop the spawn because the spawn never checks a token. The only launch guarded by the one-shot ExecutorLaunch primitive is the studio dev process.
findings.minimum_repair: Immediately before each agent/child-agent spawn (codex.rs run_with_timeout and pipeline.rs run_with_stdin), issue an ExecutorLaunch effect from the active canonical grant and call verify_authorized_effect (single_use) with the spawn target scope; abort the spawn on any rejection. Wire the canonical grant through the lifecycle driver so this token exists.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a test where an ExecutorLaunch token record is pre-marked status='consumed' (or expired/revoked) for the run; assert the agent spawn path returns an authorization error and never calls Command::spawn. Second test: two dispatches of the same run_id must not both spawn (second is EFFECT_TOKEN_ALREADY_CONSUMED).

findings.claim: Child/executor agents are spawned inheriting the full parent process environment; no .env_clear() is applied on any agent spawn path. build_executor_command (codex.rs:416-452) constructs Command::new(executor_bin) and only adds args + configure_process_group; it never clears or scrubs the environment. Grep for env_clear across lifecycle_executor and the kernel lifecycle/workflow/pipeline spawn paths returns none; the only .env() calls set OCTON_* flags additively (e.g. workflow_leaf.rs:438, lifecycle_program.rs:9652,21909-21912). The pipeline agent spawn (run_with_stdin, pipeline.rs:1846-1866) likewise never clears env.
findings.consequence: FD-022's required proof 'children cannot gain credentials' is contradicted: any credential present in the parent runtime environment (provider API keys, tokens) is inherited by the spawned Claude/Codex child by default. Agents are not credentialless, undermining the credentialless-agent + separate-broker model.
findings.minimum_repair: Apply Command::env_clear() on every agent/child-agent spawn and inject only an explicit allowlist of non-credential env vars (OCTON_* run context, PATH); route any durable credential use through a separate broker rather than inherited env.
findings.acceptance_test: Set a sentinel secret env var (e.g. FAKE_PROVIDER_KEY) in the kernel process, spawn an executor via the lifecycle path, and assert the child's environment does not contain FAKE_PROVIDER_KEY.

findings.claim: No semantic delegation-depth guard exists anywhere in the runtime. Grep for delegation_depth/invocation_depth/agent_depth/max_delegation/spawn_depth/nesting_depth/child_depth across the crates and framework returns nothing. The 'depth' occurrences found are filesystem-traversal recursion limits (lifecycle.rs:2531-2542 postmortem file collection; lifecycle_program.rs:6444-6453 evidence collection; token_budget.rs:225-226 min_depth/max_depth are a budget ladder, not delegation depth). max_child_concurrency (lifecycle.rs:181, lifecycle_program.rs) bounds PARALLELISM, not delegation nesting depth.
findings.consequence: FD-022's required proof 'children cannot exceed delegation depth' has no enforcement primitive. A child agent could in principle drive further lifecycle runs that spawn further agents without any bound on nesting depth, only a per-run step budget and concurrency cap.
findings.minimum_repair: Introduce a delegation-depth counter threaded through the ExecutionRequest/LifecycleRouteExecutionRequest (parent_run_ref chain), enforced in authorize_execution and at spawn: deny when depth exceeds a configured maximum.
findings.acceptance_test: Configure max delegation depth = N; drive a chain of nested lifecycle dispatches and assert the (N+1)th nested spawn is denied with a depth-exceeded reason code.

findings.claim: For agent routes, the effective write scope is derived and retained by the same self-attesting plane (authorization.rs declared_write_scope at 517-537 + authorized_promotion_targets at 542-613) and is NOT enforced by a consumed canonical grant scope envelope at spawn. The scope envelope enforcement (scope_matches, effects.rs:451-466) only runs inside verify_authorized_effect, which the agent spawn path never invokes (see A-02). The child agent inherits the parent repo_root as current_dir (codex.rs:449 current_dir(repo_root)) and codex is launched with --sandbox workspace-write over the whole repo plus additional --add-dir workspace dirs (codex.rs:424-437).
findings.consequence: FD-022's 'children cannot widen scope' is only advisory for agent routes: the declared write scope is recorded in a self-written proof, not enforced by a canonical single-use guard whose scope envelope gates the spawn. The codex sandbox is workspace-write over repo_root, so the OS-level boundary is the whole repo, not a narrowed child scope.
findings.minimum_repair: Bind the spawn to a verified ExecutorLaunch token whose scope envelope is the narrowed child write set, and set the executor sandbox/current_dir/add-dir to that narrowed scope rather than repo_root.
findings.acceptance_test: Issue an ExecutorLaunch token scoped to a subdirectory; assert the spawned executor is confined to that subdirectory (add-dir/sandbox root equals the token scope) and a write outside it is blocked.

findings.claim: The constitutional role model (roles.yml) is a three-class model (human / harness / model with subroles), not the FD-015 four-role TCB model (authorize / perform / verify-attest / activate-recover). The only 'four roles' in the framework are cognition/coordination roles (Orchestrator/Implementer/Archivist/Verifier) declared as HAS SHOULD in the artifact-surface technical-specification (line 688), which are documentation agents, not a TCB accounting. No artifact enumerates every physical writer as a TCB accounting (grep for 'physical writer'/'durable writer'/writer registry in framework+instance returns only a build-cache header under target/).
findings.consequence: FD-015's 'four understandable roles ... list every physical writer' is not represented as a canonical TCB model. The authorize role (authority_engine) and verify role (validator_plane) are present in substance, but 'perform' and 'activate/recover' are not distinguished as TCB roles, and no enumerated physical-writer list exists to support the 'change cannot approve/activate itself' proof obligation.
findings.minimum_repair: Add a constitutional TCB artifact mapping the four roles (authorize=authority_engine, perform=the effect-consuming writers, verify/attest=validator_plane/effect verifier, activate/recover=trust-root activation + rollback) and enumerate every physical writer (kernel command paths, pipeline stages, lifecycle executor, studio) with its role and gate.
findings.acceptance_test: A governance check parses the TCB artifact, confirms all four roles are present, and asserts every code path that performs a durable write is listed as a physical writer with a named gate.

findings.claim: For the kernel command / workflow / pipeline / service / studio paths, authorize_execution (execution.rs:2000) IS the single canonical authority: it verifies runtime route bundle freshness (2013-2083), intent binding (2085-2095), policy mode vs environment (2102-2147), executor profile + write scope preconditions (2149-2178), context-evidence binding subordinate to authorize_execution (2209-2216, enforced at 514-519), and returns a GrantBundle; downstream mutations consume single-use AuthorizedEffect tokens via verify_authorized_effect (effects.rs:210-667) which enforces decision=Allow, id/route/scope/freshness/expiry/revocation/approval/exception/rollback/budget/egress and single-use consumption. All non-test callers of authorize_execution are in kernel (commands/mod.rs, stdio.rs, workflow.rs, pipeline.rs).
findings.consequence: FD-003 is genuinely satisfied for the kernel command/pipeline/service/studio surfaces and the token verifier is a strong, reusable single-use guard primitive. The gap is confined to the lifecycle route executor plane (A-01/A-02), so the fix is to extend the existing canonical primitive to the agent-spawn path rather than build a new one.
findings.minimum_repair: No change to this primitive; reuse it. Route the lifecycle agent-spawn path through authorize_execution + verify_authorized_effect::<ExecutorLaunch> so the one existing canonical authority governs agent launches too.
findings.acceptance_test: Enumerate every process-creating call site (Command::spawn/status/output) in the runtime and assert each consequential one is dominated by a prior verify_authorized_effect on the active grant.

decision_alignment.rationale: authority_engine::authorize_execution is the sole canonical authority for the kernel command/workflow/pipeline/service/studio surfaces, and its single-use AuthorizedEffect verifier is strong (A-07). BUT the lifecycle route executor implements a SECOND, self-attesting authority plane (authorize_before_dispatch building its own DelegationProof from caller-supplied invocation_authority) and never consumes a canonical grant; lifecycle_executor does not even depend on authority_engine (A-01). The agent-spawning kernel driver (lifecycle_driver/lifecycle/lifecycle_program) contains zero references to authorize_execution. So authorize_execution is NOT the sole source of execution authority for the agent-execution path.

The one-shot invocation-guard primitive exists (ExecutorLaunch, single_use=true, consumed in verify_authorized_effect with status='consumed'), but it is issued+verified at exactly one site that launches the 'octon studio' dev process, NOT an agent. Every real agent/child-agent spawn (codex.rs:254 run_with_timeout; pipeline.rs:1856 run_with_stdin) occurs with no ExecutorLaunch token issued or consumed immediately before process creation, and no grant consumption at all on the lifecycle path. Thus 'every agent and child-agent launch consumes an exact one-shot invocation guard immediately before process creation' is not met for the launches that matter.

Substance of authorize (authority_engine) and verify/attest (validator_plane + effect token verifier) exists, but the canonical role model (roles.yml) is a three-class model (human/harness/model), not the FD-015 four roles authorize/perform/verify-attest/activate-recover, and 'perform' and 'activate/recover' are not distinguished as TCB roles. No artifact enumerates every physical writer as a TCB accounting; the only 'four roles' present are advisory cognition coordination roles in the artifact-surface technical-specification.

Child agents are NOT credentialless: no .env_clear() on any spawn path, so children inherit the full parent environment including any provider credentials (A-03). No delegation-depth guard exists anywhere; only per-run step budget and max_child_concurrency (parallelism) are enforced (A-04). Child write scope for agent routes is recorded in a self-written DelegationProof, not enforced by a consumed canonical guard, and codex runs with --sandbox workspace-write over repo_root (A-05). Therefore the required proof 'children cannot gain credentials or exceed delegation depth' (and largely 'cannot widen scope') is not enforced.

strengths_to_preserve: authority_engine::authorize_execution (execution.rs:2000) is a genuinely strong single canonical authority for kernel command/workflow/pipeline/service/studio surfaces: it verifies route-bundle freshness, intent binding, policy-mode-vs-environment, executor profile + write-scope preconditions, and subordinate context evidence before returning a GrantBundle.

The AuthorizedEffect single-use token primitive (authorized_effects/src/lib.rs, single_use + expires_at fields) plus verify_authorized_effect (effects.rs:210-667) is exactly the one-shot, exact, expiring, revocable guard FD-004 wants: it enforces decision=Allow, id/route/scope/freshness/expiry/revocation/approval/exception/rollback/budget/egress binding and marks single_use records 'consumed' atomically (effects.rs:649-658) with EFFECT_TOKEN_ALREADY_CONSUMED replay protection. Reuse this for agent launches rather than inventing a new guard.

ExecutorLaunch is already a defined EffectKind wired through issue_executor_launch_effect and verify_bundle_for_kind, and is correctly consumed for the studio launch (commands/mod.rs:735-745) — the plumbing to gate agent launches already exists and only needs to be invoked on the agent-spawn path.

The lifecycle executor already fails closed on many preconditions (delegation_contract validation, evidence gates, context binding, required receipts before dispatch, promotion-target path-escape rejection at authorization.rs:593-607) — a solid enforcement scaffold to hang canonical-grant consumption onto.

Process-group isolation and forced-kill cleanup on cancellation/timeout (codex.rs configure_process_group / force_kill_process_group) give a real basis for terminal child retirement once credential isolation is added.
uncertainties: I did not build or run the crates (read-only, target/ excluded), so all consumption/spawn-ordering claims are static; A-01/A-02 are CONFIRMED by control-flow reading but not dynamically executed.

I did not exhaustively enumerate EVERY Command::spawn/status/output call site across all 13 crates and 98k-LOC kernel; I traced the agent-spawn paths (lifecycle_executor codex/claude, kernel pipeline run_codex/run_claude, studio) and the authorize_execution callers, but there may be additional process-creation sites (e.g. in workflow.rs beyond the two I sampled) not individually verified.

Whether any runtime-effective route bundle or executor-profile config imposes an env allowlist at the OS/profile layer (outside the Rust spawn code) was not fully audited; ExecutorCommandSpec/profile in policy.rs (build_executor_command) was located but its full body (env handling, sandbox flags) was not read line-by-line — a residual chance it scrubs env that I did not observe. Grep for env_clear across the spawn paths returned none, which argues against this.

FD-015 'physical writer' enumeration may exist under an instance governance path I did not grep exhaustively; my search covered .octon/framework and .octon/instance for the obvious terms and found none outside build cache.

The handoff intake (research-input-only) frames FD-004 around a 'broker' performing durable effects; I did not assess broker existence (out of my authority/lifecycle scope) beyond confirming no broker/sqlite/WAL symbols in source per the lead's orientation.

results.subagent: Subagent B — Isolation, Credentials, Broker Boundary (FD-006, FD-008, FD-016)

findings.claim: The lifecycle executor spawns candidate work (codex/claude/auto) as a direct child process with NO OS-level sandbox and NO environment scrubbing. build_executor_command uses Command::new(executor_bin) with current_dir(repo_root) (the CANONICAL repo), never calls env_clear/env_remove, and only passes flags to the executor CLI itself. For codex it passes the Codex CLI's own '--sandbox workspace-write'; for claude it passes only '-p --output-format text' with NO sandbox flag whatsoever. The child therefore inherits the full parent environment (any GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, git credentials) and runs against the canonical working tree.
findings.consequence: Any agent process launched by the lifecycle executor runs with full ambient credentials and full canonical-repo write access mediated only by the third-party executor CLI's own sandbox (codex) or by nothing at all (claude). A compromised or misbehaving prompt can read GITHUB_TOKEN/SSH keys from the inherited env and reach network/filesystem outside any Octon-enforced envelope. This directly contradicts FD-006 (agents credentialless) and FD-008 (native OS sandboxing).
findings.minimum_repair: Before spawn, clear the environment (Command::env_clear) and re-inject only an explicit allowlist that excludes all durable credentials; wrap the child in an OS sandbox (macOS sandbox-exec/App Sandbox profile) enforced by the runtime rather than trusting the executor CLI's own flag; make the claude path also apply a sandbox posture.
findings.acceptance_test: A test that builds the executor command for both codex and claude and asserts (a) env is cleared and only an allowlist without GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/SSH_AUTH_SOCK remains, and (b) the spawned command is wrapped by a runtime-owned OS sandbox invocation; plus an adversarial test that a child cannot read a sentinel secret env var set in the parent.

findings.claim: There is NO separate local deterministic broker process that holds durable credentials. The only artifact named 'broker' in the repo is .octon/framework/capabilities/_ops/scripts/policy-grant-broker.sh, which brokers capability GRANT RECORDS (JSON files with tools/write-scopes/TTL/provenance) via a policy runner — it never holds, issues, or handles any durable credential (no GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH key, or secret). No 'launch broker' or 'local effect broker' component exists in the Rust runtime source.
findings.consequence: FD-006's core primitive — a single separate local deterministic broker that alone holds durable credentials so agents/executors stay credentialless — does not exist. Durable credentials remain wherever the host puts them (ambient env, gh keychain) and are inherited by every spawned agent. The grant-broker only records authorization intent, so it provides no credential custody boundary.
findings.minimum_repair: Introduce an actual credential-custody broker process (separate from the agent/executor process) that holds durable credentials, and route all credentialed effects (git push, gh, deploy) through typed broker operations that agents invoke without ever receiving the raw secret; keep the policy-grant-broker as the authorization layer feeding it.
findings.acceptance_test: Integration test: with all credential env vars unset in the agent/executor process, a git-push or gh operation still succeeds because it is performed by the broker, and a test asserting the executor child process never has any credential env var present.

findings.claim: There is a SECOND executor spawn path in the kernel pipeline (authority_engine build_executor_command) whose Codex invocation omits the '--sandbox' flag entirely and, when the executor profile has dangerous_flags_allowed=true, adds '--full-auto' (codex) or '--permission-mode bypassPermissions' (claude). Like the lifecycle path it uses current_dir(repo_root) and performs no env scrubbing. The 'release_candidate_preparation' default profile has dangerous_flags_allowed=true.
findings.consequence: Two divergent executor spawn paths exist with inconsistent sandbox posture: the pipeline/authority_engine path applies NO sandbox flag to codex at all (unlike the lifecycle path's '--sandbox workspace-write'), and under a dangerous profile actively grants full-auto/bypassPermissions. Neither scrubs credentials. This is a wider hole than the lifecycle path and further contradicts FD-008/FD-006. The inconsistency also makes the effective isolation posture depend on which code path launched the agent.
findings.minimum_repair: Unify both spawn paths through a single sandbox-and-env-scrubbing wrapper; ensure the authority_engine codex path also gets an enforced sandbox; gate dangerous_flags_allowed behind an OS-enforced envelope so 'bypassPermissions' cannot also mean 'ambient credentials + canonical repo'.
findings.acceptance_test: A test asserting both build_executor_command implementations (lifecycle_executor and authority_engine) produce a command wrapped by the same runtime-owned sandbox and with a cleared/allowlisted env, and that no code path can spawn an executor without that wrapper.

findings.claim: No OS-level sandbox or isolation primitive exists anywhere in the repository (excluding target/): a repo-wide grep for sandbox-exec, seatbelt, unshare, chroot, nsjail, bubblewrap/bwrap, firejail, seccomp, setrlimit, pledge, unveil returns ZERO matches. The only cfg(target_os) usage is in studio/src/app_state.rs for clipboard and reveal-in-file-manager helpers (pbcopy/open, wl-copy/xdg-open, powershell/explorer), not for candidate-work isolation. The string 'sandbox' in runtime source is either a passed-through Codex CLI flag or a replay-store comment ('sandbox replay keeps side effects isolated').
findings.consequence: FD-008's 'macOS native sandboxing' is entirely ABSENT from the codebase. There is no seatbelt/App Sandbox profile, no namespace/OCI isolation, no host-conformance suite. The runtime provides zero OS-enforced isolation of candidate work; it relies wholly on the third-party executor CLIs' self-declared sandbox flags.
findings.minimum_repair: Implement a macOS sandbox-exec/App Sandbox profile applied by the runtime at spawn (with an explicit filesystem/network/process envelope), plus a conformance/escape-denial test suite as the trust boundary; treat Linux path as experimental and explicitly refuse to launch on unsupported platforms.
findings.acceptance_test: On macOS, an escape test where an agent attempts to write outside its declared write-scope or open a disallowed network endpoint is denied by the runtime-applied sandbox profile (not merely by the executor CLI), with a retained escape-denial evidence envelope.

findings.claim: Candidate work is NOT run in an isolated worktree/clone with separate .git objects/refs; it runs in the canonical repository. Every executor spawn sets current_dir(repo_root) on the canonical repo root (codex --cd repo_root, current_dir(repo_root); claude current_dir; workflow_leaf current_dir(repo_root)). 'worktree' appears in the source only in the kernel's closeout/hygiene classification that DETECTS foreign/ambiguous worktrees after the fact — it does not CREATE an isolated worktree for candidate execution. No GIT_DIR override or git-clone-for-isolation exists in the runtime.
findings.consequence: FD-008's 'isolated Git state' is not implemented. Candidate agents operate directly on canonical .git objects and refs, so a misbehaving agent can create/move refs, stage, and commit against the canonical repository with no object-store isolation. The only protection is after-the-fact worktree-hygiene detection during closeout, not prevention.
findings.minimum_repair: Launch candidate work in a disposable worktree/clone with an isolated GIT_DIR (or a separate object store), and only promote reviewed trees/refs into canonical state through the effect broker; keep the hygiene classifier as a backstop.
findings.acceptance_test: A test that a candidate run's git writes land in a disposable object store/worktree and that the canonical repo's refs and objects are unchanged until an explicit brokered promotion step runs.

findings.claim: Credential custody is entirely delegated to host tools and the ambient environment; no Octon-owned vault/keyring exists. connector-credentials.yml declares storage_posture values 'no_credentials' and 'externally_managed' with default_route: deny and credential_policy_authorizes_execution: false — i.e. the policy explicitly defers durable credential storage to external managers. No keyring/secret-service/security-framework crate dependency exists in any runtime Cargo.toml. The gh CLI is invoked via gh_output inheriting ambient env; the github-autonomy-runbook documents that gh reads auth from the macOS Keychain (gh's own keyring), confirming credentials live in host-tool custody, not an Octon broker.
findings.consequence: The design intent (per connector-credentials.yml) is that Octon holds NO durable credentials — they are externally managed. But because there is no broker mediating credentialed effects and no env scrubbing before agent spawn, those externally-managed credentials are reachable by any spawned agent through the ambient environment (gh keychain unlocks in the inherited session, SSH agent socket inherited). FD-006's separation (broker holds credentials, agents credentialless) is therefore neither implemented nor enforceable at the spawn boundary.
findings.minimum_repair: Keep credentials externally managed but interpose the credential-custody broker so agents never inherit the ambient credential surface; scrub SSH_AUTH_SOCK/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN and any gh keychain reachability from the executor child env, and require credentialed effects to go through typed broker calls.
findings.acceptance_test: With the executor child launched, assert 'gh auth status' inside the child fails (no inherited keychain/token) while a brokered gh operation initiated by the runtime succeeds; assert SSH_AUTH_SOCK is absent in the child env.

findings.claim: authorize_before_dispatch self-attests authorization: it builds and writes its own DelegationProof YAML (with a self-constructed invocation_authority map) and never calls a kernel verify_authorized_effect for the ExecutorLaunch. ExecutorLaunch exists only as a classification label (MaterialSideEffectClass::ExecutorLaunch) used for metadata, with no unavoidable in-kernel gate at the spawn site. The one callback that does re-enter the kernel (admit_existing_lifecycle_run) shells out to the SAME runtime binary via std::env::current_exe() with current_dir(repo_root), inheriting the same environment — it is not a separate credentialless boundary and only runs for route_id == run-packet-implementation.
findings.consequence: The ExecutorLaunch side effect has no unavoidable mediated boundary: the executor authorizes itself by writing a proof file, so the isolation/credential guarantees FD-006/FD-016 depend on are self-asserted rather than broker-verified. A code path that skips authorize_before_dispatch (or a divergent spawn path such as the pipeline path in B-03) can launch an agent with no proof at all, and there is no kernel chokepoint that refuses an unproven ExecutorLaunch.
findings.minimum_repair: Route every executor launch through a single mediated verify step (verify_authorized_effect for a one-shot AuthorizedEffect<ExecutorLaunch>) owned by an independent broker/authority process that also installs the sandbox and scrubbed env before spawn; make spawning without a verified single-use effect impossible by construction.
findings.acceptance_test: A negative test proving no code path can spawn codex/claude without first consuming a verified single-use ExecutorLaunch effect, and that the verify step is performed by a process distinct from the one building the proof.

findings.claim: Degraded operation is narrow at the ROUTE level (FD-016's first clause is partially met): failures produce per-route blocked/failed/cancelled/preflight-blocked results with specific error classes and next_action = manual-intervention, blocking only the affected transition rather than the whole system; the codex runtime preflight blocks only that codex route. However the 'never expose ambient credentials' clause is only vacuously satisfied — there is no credential custody to protect, and ambient credentials are already exposed to every spawned child (findings B-01, B-06), so a degraded transition neither newly exposes nor withholds credentials.
findings.consequence: The transition-scoped blocking half of FD-016 is present and is a genuine strength, but the credential-protection half is unenforceable because there is no credential boundary to preserve during degradation. FD-016 cannot be fully satisfied until B-01/B-06 establish a credential boundary that degraded operation can then protect.
findings.minimum_repair: Once a credential-custody broker exists, add explicit assertions that a blocked/degraded transition leaves the credential envelope withheld from the affected executor and emits evidence that no ambient credential was surfaced.
findings.acceptance_test: Fault-injection test: force a transition into blocked state and assert the affected executor's env contains no credentials before, during, and after the block, and that only the affected route (not sibling routes) is stopped.

decision_alignment.rationale: FD-006 requires agents and lifecycle executors to be credentialless with one separate local deterministic broker holding durable credentials. The repo has NO credential-custody broker (the only 'broker' is policy-grant-broker.sh, which brokers authorization grant records, not credentials — B-02). Executors spawn candidate work with NO env scrubbing (no env_clear/env_remove anywhere in runtime crates), so children inherit the full ambient credential surface: GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/SSH_AUTH_SOCK and gh's macOS-Keychain auth (B-01, B-06). connector-credentials.yml declares credentials 'externally_managed', but nothing prevents spawned agents from reaching them. There is not even a mediated ExecutorLaunch gate — the executor self-attests via a written DelegationProof (B-07). The separation FD-006 mandates is neither implemented nor enforceable.
evidence: .octon/framework/engine/runtime/crates/authority_engine/src/implementation/policy.rs:36-69 (second spawn path, no env scrub, no sandbox on codex)

decision_alignment.rationale: FD-008 requires macOS native sandboxing plus isolated Git state (Linux experimental; VMs/Windows out). A repo-wide search found ZERO OS sandbox primitives (sandbox-exec, seatbelt, App Sandbox, unshare, chroot, seccomp, bwrap, pledge) outside target/ (B-04). The only cfg(target_os) code is studio clipboard/file-reveal helpers, unrelated to isolation. decision_alignment.rationale: FD-016 has two clauses. Clause 1 (block only the affected transition, never the whole system) is genuinely met: failures yield per-route blocked/failed/cancelled/preflight-blocked results with specific error classes and next_action=manual-intervention; the codex runtime preflight blocks only that codex route while other routes proceed (B-08). This transition-scoped fail-closed design is a real strength. Clause 2 (never expose ambient credentials during degraded operation) is only VACUOUSLY satisfied: there is no credential boundary to protect because ambient credentials are already exposed to every spawned agent regardless of degradation (B-01, B-06) and no credential-custody broker exists (B-02). So a degraded transition neither newly exposes nor withholds credentials — the clause is un-enforceable until FD-006's boundary exists. Net: the blocking-narrowness half is satisfied; the credential-protection half is not, so overall PARTIALLY_SATISFIED.

strengths_to_preserve: Transition-scoped fail-closed degradation: failures produce narrow per-route blocked/failed/cancelled/preflight-blocked results with typed error classes and next_action=manual-intervention rather than halting the whole system (adapter.rs:161-380, codex.rs:31-74) — this is the correct FD-016 blocking primitive and should be retained.

connector-credentials.yml already encodes the RIGHT intent: default_route: deny, credential_policy_authorizes_execution: false, material_execution_still_requires_run_authorization: true, and storage_posture no_credentials/externally_managed — a good policy scaffold to build the actual credential broker against (connector-credentials.yml:1-35).

The MaterialSideEffectClass::ExecutorLaunch classification and material-side-effect inventory (side_effects/mod.rs) already name ExecutorLaunch as a material side effect requiring an authorization boundary — the label exists to hang a real mediated verify on.

policy-grant-broker.sh provides a working, deterministic, evidence-emitting authorization-grant layer (create/inspect/renew/revoke/sweep with TTL and provenance) that can feed a future credential-custody broker without being conflated with it.

Executor profiles (ExecutorProfileConfig with dangerous_flags_allowed/allow_repo_write/require_hard_enforce/require_human_review) give a per-profile posture knob (config.rs:86-141) that a sandbox/env-scrub wrapper can key off.

Process-group isolation and robust termination (configure_process_group via setpgid, SIGTERM->SIGKILL group cleanup in codex.rs:520-619) already give clean teardown of the candidate process tree — a necessary precondition for a real sandbox envelope.
uncertainties: Whether GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/SSH_AUTH_SOCK are actually present in the environment at agent-spawn time is DEPLOYMENT_LOCAL (depends on the operator's shell/session); the CODE-LEVEL fact is only that the runtime does nothing to scrub them, so IF present they are inherited. I did not execute a spawn to observe the child env (no DYNAMICALLY_EXECUTED evidence).

The research proposal under .octon/inputs/additive/.incoming and the exploratory revision-2 proposal describe an elaborate target (rootless OCI/native sandbox, launch broker, effect broker, credential vault with JIT handles) — these are unverified research inputs and I treated them only as intent, not as repo facts. Notably the proposal's target ('rootless OCI, native Linux or VM-backed macOS/Windows') appears to differ from FD-008's 'macOS native sandboxing; VMs out', a possible decision-vs-research divergence worth a lead cross-check, but it does not change the ABSENT alignment since neither is implemented.

I did not exhaustively trace every kernel call site that could reach an executor spawn; I confirmed two distinct spawn paths (lifecycle_executor and authority_engine/pipeline) plus workflow_leaf, but there may be additional CLI entrypoints (e.g. studio launch, scaffold cargo) that spawn processes with the same ambient-env posture — the pattern (Command::new + current_dir + no env_clear) is uniform across all sites I inspected.

FD-016's 'never expose ambient credentials' is judged PARTIALLY_SATISFIED as vacuous; a stricter reading could call it CONTRADICTED (since degraded operation runs atop an already-credential-exposing spawn). I classified conservatively as PARTIALLY_SATISFIED because the clause is about the degradation event itself not newly exposing credentials, which is technically true even though the baseline already exposes them.

findings.claim: No credentialed-Git broker exists: every git invocation in the repo runs with the ambient environment and repo-controlled configuration. No git script, skill, or Rust caller sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, -c core.hooksPath=, or disables includes/filters/fsmonitor. `git commit` runs WITHOUT --no-verify, so pre-commit/commit-msg hooks execute. The `text=auto`/`eol=lf`/symlink `.gitattributes` at repo root is benign, but nothing prevents a candidate from committing a `.gitattributes` `filter=`/`diff=` driver or a repo-local hook that git would then honor on the operator's machine.
findings.consequence: The FD-009 guarantee that credentialed Git flows only through a broker-owned sanitized config, and that hooks/includes/filters/helpers/submodules/fsmonitor/aliases/drivers CANNOT execute, is not implemented. A candidate that lands content on a branch (or an already-merged repo state on an operator machine) can ship a malicious hook, `.gitattributes` filter/diff driver, config include, or credential helper; the next `git commit`/`git checkout`/`git diff` by the operator or the autonomy hooks will execute it with the operator's credentials and PAT in scope.
findings.minimum_repair: Introduce a single git wrapper (Rust or shell) that all mutation/query helpers must call, exporting GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (or a broker-owned config), -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null, -c core.fsmonitor=false, and -c protocol.*.allow=never for submodules, and passing --no-verify on commit/push. Add a validator that fails if any git script bypasses the wrapper.
findings.acceptance_test: grep for `Command::new("git")` and `run_cmd git`/`git -C` across .octon and .github shows every mutating invocation routed through the sanitized wrapper; a test that plants a repo-local .git/hooks/pre-commit and a `.gitattributes` filter driver and then runs git-branch-commit.sh proves neither executes.

findings.claim: The repo actively INSTALLS and USES git hooks rather than disabling them. git-autonomy-hooks-install.sh writes managed post-merge and post-checkout hooks into .git/hooks that re-invoke git-pr-cleanup.sh (which itself performs `git merge --ff-only origin/main` and ref mutations). The managed hook also chains any pre-existing `<hook>.octon-local` backup unconditionally.
findings.consequence: FD-009 requires that hooks cannot execute. The current design does the opposite: hooks are a load-bearing autonomy mechanism that runs git mutations (merge/ref writes) in the background on merge/checkout, and blindly execs a backed-up prior hook. This is both an FD-009 violation and an autonomous-mutation surface that runs outside any authorization envelope.
findings.minimum_repair: Move the post-merge/post-checkout cleanup convergence out of git hooks into an explicit, authorization-gated command the operator/agent runs deliberately; if hooks are retained, they must run under the sanitized broker with an explicit allowlist and must not chain arbitrary legacy hooks.
findings.acceptance_test: With sanitized git config in force (core.hooksPath=/dev/null), a post-merge does not spawn git-pr-cleanup; cleanup convergence still works via an explicit authorized command.

findings.claim: The exact-SHA / route-neutral verifier is candidate-controlled, not an immutable verifier separate from effect identity. The four live required status checks on main (confirmed via gh api: route_neutral_closeout_validation, branch_naming_validation, route_aware_autonomy_validation, exact_source_sha_validation) are all jobs defined in .github/workflows/change-route-projection.yml — an agent-editable file in the repo tree. The exact_source_sha_validation job passes trivially (echo 'valid for shadow/report-only') whenever no receipt_path input is supplied, which is the normal case for a PR merge (PR_HEAD_SHA path) or a raw push; it only enforces receipt/route binding on manual workflow_dispatch with an explicit receipt_path. main-change-route-guard.yml (the receipt route verifier) runs on: push with permissions: contents: read AFTER the update has already landed, so it can only report, never block. Its required-check list is read from github-control-plane-contract.json, also candidate-editable.
findings.consequence: FD-011 requires a candidate-immutable, exact-SHA verifier whose identity is separate from effect identity. Here the verifier's code, its required-check contract, and its pass/fail logic all live inside the candidate-editable repo. An admitted candidate that edits change-route-projection.yml (e.g., makes exact_source_sha_validation an unconditional success) and lands it changes the meaning of the check that gates the very landing — the verdict is authored by the thing being verified. The verifier also does not verify against a pre-computed exact SHA independent of the pushed head in the common (no-receipt) path.
findings.minimum_repair: Move the exact-SHA verifier out of the candidate tree into an out-of-band, candidate-immutable location (a GitHub App / separate protected worker repo, or a required check whose workflow lives in a repo the candidate cannot edit), keyed to a pre-registered exact SHA and route verdict computed by the authorization envelope, not re-derived from the pushed head. Make change-route-projection.yml modifications themselves require the immutable verifier to pass.
findings.acceptance_test: A candidate PR that rewrites .github/workflows/change-route-projection.yml exact_source_sha_validation to `exit 0` is blocked from landing because the immutable, out-of-tree verifier (unaffected by the candidate diff) still enforces the pre-registered SHA/route verdict.

findings.claim: No optional protected GitHub Actions effect worker with a narrowly scoped App exists. There is zero GitHub App configuration anywhere in the repo (no create-github-app-token, app_id, installation token, or private-key wiring). Provider writes (auto-merge, protected merge boundary) run inside pr-auto-merge.yml on `pull_request_target` with permissions contents: write / pull-requests: write, authenticated by `secrets.AUTONOMY_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` — a broad PAT/default token, not a narrowly scoped App. The write logic (protected-ci-auto-merge.sh, evaluate-pr-autonomy-policy.sh) is candidate-authored in the repo tree.
findings.consequence: FD-007's optional protected Actions effect worker with a narrowly scoped App is not present. Provider-write authority is a broad PAT held in a candidate-editable workflow triggered by pull_request_target (which runs with repo secrets even for the base ref); the merge policy code is candidate-authored. This is a weaker and broader capability than the FD-007 target and offers no App-scoped isolation. The local broker (git-branch-authorize/land helpers) does stay authoritative for hosted no-PR landing, so the second clause of FD-007 is met, but the App-scoped worker clause is absent.
findings.minimum_repair: If FD-007's optional worker is desired, add a narrowly scoped GitHub App (least-privilege, contents+pull_requests only, single-repo installation) minted via create-github-app-token, and keep its policy code out of the candidate-editable tree; otherwise mark FD-007's worker clause explicitly out of scope and ensure the PAT-based auto-merge is gated by the immutable verifier from C-003.
findings.acceptance_test: pr-auto-merge.yml authenticates via a scoped App installation token (not AUTONOMY_PAT), the App has only contents/pull-requests write on this repo, and disabling the App leaves the local broker landing path fully functional.

findings.claim: route_selection_order lists direct-main BEFORE branch-no-pr, and direct-main permits autonomous agents to land and push directly on main. default-work-unit.yml route_selection_order is: resolve identity, fail_closed, branch-pr (predicate), direct-main, branch-no-pr, stage-only-escalate. solo_route_selection.direct_main_first_when_all explicitly prefers direct-main for solo low-risk changes; the direct-main route description says it is 'landed directly on current clean main and pushed to origin'.
findings.consequence: FD-010 requires a verified branch-no-PR default for admitted Class B, automatic PR escalation, and that agents NEVER work/publish directly on main. The current contract makes direct-main the PREFERRED solo route (ordered above branch-no-pr and chosen first when clean-main predicates hold), i.e. autonomous agents ARE expected to commit and push directly on main. This directly contradicts the FD-010 'agents NEVER work/publish directly on main' clause and inverts the intended branch-no-pr default ordering.
findings.minimum_repair: For admitted Class B autonomous agents, remove direct-main from the autonomous route order (or gate it behind an operator-only predicate), make branch-no-pr the default, and require automatic escalation to branch-pr on the FD-010-defined conditions. Keep direct-main only for explicit human/solo-maintainer operation.
findings.acceptance_test: route_selection_order for the autonomous Class B profile lists branch-no-pr before/without direct-main; a solo low-risk autonomous change selects branch-no-pr and never commits on main; validate-default-work-unit-alignment.sh enforces the new ordering.

findings.claim: Live protected main is route-neutral: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/main` returns rule types [deletion, required_status_checks, non_fast_forward, required_linear_history] with NO pull_request rule. Required status check contexts are exactly [route_neutral_closeout_validation, branch_naming_validation, route_aware_autonomy_validation, exact_source_sha_validation] — the four candidate-authored jobs from change-route-projection.yml.
findings.consequence: The only non-cooperative (provider-enforced) boundary protecting main is the ruleset, and it enforces exactly four checks whose defining workflows are candidate-editable (see C-003). Non-fast-forward + linear history genuinely prevent force-push/history rewrite, but the semantic gate (route/receipt/exact-SHA correctness) is delegated to candidate-authored checks. This confirms the ruleset is the sole hard boundary and that it is only as strong as the candidate-authored check jobs behind it.
findings.minimum_repair: Bind the required status check contexts to workflows hosted outside the candidate-editable tree (per C-003), so the provider-enforced gate cannot be neutered by a candidate diff.
findings.acceptance_test: The required_status_checks contexts on main resolve to workflows the candidate cannot edit; a candidate diff to .github/workflows cannot weaken any required check.

findings.claim: The hosted no-PR landing broker resolves the GitHub owner/repo and provider ruleset from repo-controlled state: github_repo() parses `git remote get-url origin`, and ruleset_requires_pr_live() queries whatever remote that resolves to. A candidate that controls the remote URL (via config include or a committed .gitmodules/remote rewrite) could redirect ruleset inspection to an attacker-controlled repo whose rules report no PR requirement.
findings.consequence: Compounds FD-009/FD-011: because git runs with unsanitized config (C-001), the remote and ruleset provenance the preflight trusts are themselves candidate-influenceable, so the 'provider ruleset allows route-neutral landing' verdict can be spoofed. The narrow command surface intent (no PR create/merge in these helpers) is partially met — the helpers deliberately never create/merge PRs — but the provenance is not pinned.
findings.minimum_repair: Pin the target owner/repo and the ruleset query endpoint in broker-owned config (not derived from repo-controlled remote), and run the query with sanitized git config so config includes cannot rewrite the remote.
findings.acceptance_test: Rewriting `origin` remote URL via a repo-local config include does not change which repo/ruleset the hosted preflight inspects.
