Rename the retention 'Class A/B/C' to a distinct term (e.g. Retention Tier 1/2/3) to remove the naming collision.
findings.acceptance_test: grep the repo for a contract that binds the strings 'Class A'/'Class B'/'Class C' to autonomous/brokered/stronger-controls routing (not retention). A representative 'Class A' task must show zero routine prompts and a 'Class C' task must be provably unable to select a lower route, referencing the same named buckets FD-002 uses.

findings.claim: There is NO local credentialed broker implemented as a runtime process/binary. FD-024 lists 'local broker' as a required deliverable and FD-006 requires 'one separate local deterministic broker holding durable credentials'. Grep across all Rust crates for broker / credential-holder / credential-vault returns nothing; the only 'broker' artifact is a shell script policy-grant-broker.sh that mints policy grants, not a credential-holding daemon. Agents/executors being credentialless is therefore unenforced by any broker boundary.
symbol_refs: DelegateCmd (lease commands, not a broker process)
findings.consequence: The central privilege boundary FD-024/FD-006 depend on does not exist as a runtime component. Without a credential-holding broker, 'agents are credentialless' and 'raw push/merge/deploy fail from candidate execution' cannot be demonstrated. This is the single largest FD-024 gap: the vertical 'complete path' is missing its authority anchor. It also feeds the mediation gap (H-03): even the in-kernel authorization is not invoked at launch, and there is no broker to hold credentials that agents must go through.
findings.minimum_repair: Introduce a single local broker component (process or in-kernel role) that holds durable provider credentials, exposes a narrow deterministic effect surface, and is the only holder of push/merge/deploy capability; make agent and lifecycle-executor launch paths credentialless by construction.
findings.acceptance_test: Negative test: a candidate execution attempting raw git push / PR merge / deployment / protected access without going through the broker fails. Positive test: the same effect succeeds only when routed through the broker with a valid grant.

findings.claim: authority_engine's verify_authorized_effect is only ever called from within authority_engine itself (implementation.rs, effects.rs) and its tests — never from the kernel/executor launch paths (ExecutorLaunch). Meanwhile lifecycle_executor/src/authorization.rs::authorize_before_dispatch BUILDS AND WRITES its own DelegationProof via build_and_write_proof, constructing its own invocation_authority checks. So there are two authority planes and no unavoidable mediation boundary at process launch.
findings.consequence: For FD-002 (Class A must run with zero routine prompts) and FD-024 (safe self-dev, no unauthorized durable effects), the safety property is asserted by governance prose and by an executor-self-constructed proof rather than enforced at an unavoidable kernel boundary. A solo operator relying on 'Class A is autonomous but bounded' has no single choke point proving effects were authorized. This is architectural inference about enforceability, corroborated by the standing repo memory note on the mediation gap.
findings.minimum_repair: Make process/effect launch call the canonical authority_engine verify path (or the broker from H-02) as an unavoidable mediation step; retire the executor's self-built DelegationProof as a competing authority source (reduce it to evidence, not authority).
findings.acceptance_test: Grep shows every ExecutorLaunch/effect-dispatch path routes through a single authorize/verify call; a launch with missing/forged/stale/revoked authority is denied before process creation regardless of executor-local proof.

findings.claim: There is a substantial cross-org / federated-trust subsystem that conflicts with FD-001's 'one serious solo operator; enterprise/team administration out of scope'. The kernel ships Trust-domain registry, Trust Compacts (propose/approve/revoke), Federation ledger/status, Attestation (verify/accept/reject), Delegated-authority Leases, and portable Proof-bundle import/export — trust.rs alone is ~1,515 LOC, and these are top-level CLI verbs (Trust, Proof, Attest, Delegate, Certify, Federation). This is multi-party trust-federation machinery a single operator with separate technical identities does not need.
findings.consequence: This is the clearest scope-conflicting subsystem for FD-001. Federation compacts and cross-domain trust are inherently multi-party; they add ~1.5k+ LOC of surface, several CLI verb families, and their own contracts/state for a persona that is explicitly one person. It inflates install/operate/diagnose burden (the FD-001 required proof) and dilutes the 'one complete vertical path' FD-024 wants. Note: some of this could be defended as future provider-native delegation (FD-023), but trust COMPACTS and FEDERATION LEDGERS are multi-operator constructs, not solo primitives.
findings.minimum_repair: Gate Trust-domain / Federation / Trust-Compact behind an off-by-default feature or move it out of the solo vertical; retain only the single-operator-relevant pieces (attestation verify, proof export/import for self-dogfooding) if any. Confirm with the operator which trust verbs are load-bearing for a solo build.
findings.acceptance_test: With federation/trust-compact disabled, the solo dogfood mission set (FD-024 required proof) still completes end to end. No solo workflow depends on TrustCompactCmd or FederationCmd.

findings.claim: There is no 'CLI mission inbox' as FD-024 names it. The closest surface is the Mission Queue (octon mission queue / mission next) which is per-mission action-slice selection, and Decision Request inspection (octon decide list/resolve). There is no cross-mission operator inbox aggregating pending items/decisions across the operator's multiple projects. The word 'inbox' in-repo refers only to the human scratchpad staging folder (ideation/scratchpad/inbox), not a mission control surface.
findings.consequence: FD-024's 'CLI mission inbox' as the operator's daily driver across multiple projects is only partially present: per-mission queue + decision list exist, but there is no unified inbox view spanning projects/missions. For a solo operator managing multiple projects, the absence of a single 'what needs me now across everything' surface raises daily operating burden (the FD-001/FD-024 proof obligation).
findings.minimum_repair: Add a cross-mission/cross-project inbox command (e.g. octon inbox) that aggregates open Decision Requests, blocked slices, and escalations across all missions/projects into one operator-facing list, reusing the existing DecisionRequest and Mission Queue primitives.
findings.acceptance_test: octon inbox (or equivalent) lists all pending operator decisions and blocked items across every active mission/project in one call; resolving from that surface advances the underlying missions.

findings.claim: The Project Profile is singular per repo (.octon/instance/locality/project-profile.yml), and Engagements bind one Project Profile each. FD-024/FD-019 require multi-project support ('multiple projects', 'multi-project continuity'). There is no durable multi-project registry/identity record in the Rust source; grep for workspace-project / multi-project / project-identity in crates returns only the single PROJECT_PROFILE_REF constant.
findings.consequence: The 'multiple projects' pillar of FD-024 (and FD-019's minimal durable project identity/boundary record) is not visibly realized: the runtime models one project profile per .octon root. Whether multi-project is achieved by multiple .octon roots (one per repo) or a single registry is unverified — but no Workspace-Project identity record exists in code, so multi-project continuity is undemonstrated. UNCERTAIN whether the intended model is many independent .octon installs vs. one operator workspace.
findings.minimum_repair: Either document/prove that multi-project = one .octon per repo with a lightweight operator-level index, or add the FD-019 minimal durable project identity/boundary record (never authority) so multiple projects share one operator surface.
findings.acceptance_test: An operator with N repos can enumerate and continue missions across all N from one surface; project metadata provably cannot widen an active run or mint authority (FD-019 proof).

findings.claim: Operate/maintain surface is very large for one person: 13 Rust crates (~157k LOC across crates), 42 GitHub workflows (many governance gates: adr-prompt, ai-review-gate, alignment-check, architecture-conformance, assurance-weight-gates, closure-certification, deny-by-default-gates, principles-charter-overrides-audit, uec-cutover-certify/validate, unified-execution-constitution-closure, etc.), 33 instance governance policies, ~2,342 framework config/doc files, plus .octon/state (~148.6k files) and .octon/generated (~36.6k files). FD-001's required proof is that ONE person can install, operate, upgrade, diagnose, and recover Octon within burden targets.
findings.consequence: The internal-complexity exposure and monthly admin burden are high relative to a solo persona. 42 CI workflows (a large fraction being certification/closure/charter-audit gates) plus 33 governance policies plus 185k state+generated files is an operating platform, not a single-person tool. This directly stresses the FD-001 burden targets and the FD-024 'low review burden' proof. The 148k state + 36k generated files also imply heavy repository churn that a solo operator must keep coherent.
findings.minimum_repair: Define explicit burden targets (install steps, workflows a solo run actually triggers, monthly maintenance minutes) and trim non-load-bearing gates. Candidate cuts for the solo vertical: UEC cutover/closure certification workflows, charter-overrides-audit, assurance-weight-gates, and federation-related CI, unless each maps to a testable safety property in the solo path.
findings.acceptance_test: A fresh macOS install-to-first-mission runbook has a bounded, measured step count; a routine Class A/B change triggers only the small subset of workflows tied to a named safety property, and the rest are quarantined behind self-dev/enterprise flags.

findings.claim: The autonomy policy imposes machine quorum for medium/high tiers: ACP-2 requires 2 signers (execution agent + independent verifier/validator), ACP-3 requires 3, ACP-4 requires human/break-glass. risk-materiality maps ordinary repo mutation (git.commit / mutate_repo) to ACP-2 with required_route 'escalate' and required approval artifacts (decision-artifact + grant-bundle). For a solo operator, routine repo commits mapping to an escalate route with 2-party quorum is exactly the 'false escalation / ceremony' risk the simplification lens is asked to flag.
symbol_refs: risk-materiality tiers repo-change-moderate risk_tier ACP-2 required_route escalate
findings.consequence: FD-002 promises Class A/B run autonomously with zero routine prompts. But the risk-materiality contract routes ordinary repo mutation to ACP-2/escalate with a 2-party quorum and grant-bundle/decision-artifact requirements. If enforced literally, a solo operator's routine commits generate escalation ceremony and prompts — the opposite of FD-002's 'zero routine prompts for Class A/B'. Whether this ceremony actually fires for solo commits depends on how mission_class defaults + proceed_on_silence interact (mode_defaults maintenance='notify', reconcile='proceed_on_silence'), which softens but does not remove the escalate route. This tension needs a concrete solo-path resolution.
findings.minimum_repair: Reconcile risk-materiality's 'repo-change-moderate -> escalate + quorum 2' with FD-002's 'Class B brokered + auto-completed, zero routine prompts'. Define a solo profile where reversible repo mutation on an isolated branch with independent exact-SHA verification (FD-011) satisfies the ACP-2 quorum via the verifier as the second party — no human prompt.
findings.acceptance_test: A representative reversible repo change on an isolated branch completes with zero human prompts, with the independent SHA verifier counted as the second quorum member; a genuinely higher-consequence (ACP-3+/destructive) change provably cannot take that route.

findings.claim: The `octon doctor` command exists but only supports `--architecture` (runs validate-architecture-health.sh, a self-development gate) and hard-errors without that flag. There is no operator-facing setup/health/recover 'doctor' that diagnoses a solo operator's install (broker up, credentials present, missions healthy, storage capacity). FD-001 requires proof one person can install, diagnose, and recover.
findings.consequence: The diagnose/recover leg of the FD-001 burden proof is only partly served: doctor is a self-dev architecture linter, not an operator health check. A solo operator hitting a broken install/broker/credential/storage state has no first-class diagnostic path, raising recovery burden.
findings.minimum_repair: Add an operator-mode doctor (no --architecture) that checks broker/credential presence, mission/queue integrity, evidence storage capacity (FD-013), and offers recovery hints; keep the architecture gate as a separate self-dev subcommand.
findings.acceptance_test: octon doctor (no flags) reports install health across broker, credentials, missions, and storage, and returns non-zero with actionable output when any is broken.

decision_alignment.rationale: Positive: no RBAC/SSO/SCIM/multi-tenant/raft/consensus/kubernetes/distributed-VM subsystem exists in the runtime (grep across framework/instance/crates excluding target found only skill-guidance docs and a Postgres best-practices note, none of which are load-bearing subsystems). A single-operator CLI (octon), single Project Profile, and mission model are present. Negative: a substantial cross-org federated-trust subsystem (Trust-domain registry, Trust Compacts, Federation ledger, Attestation, Delegated leases; ~1.5k LOC in trust.rs plus top-level CLI verbs) is multi-party by nature and conflicts with 'enterprise/team administration out of scope' (H-04). The operate/maintain surface (13 crates ~157k LOC, 42 workflows, 33 policies, ~185k state+generated files) is large for one person and the install/diagnose/recover proof is only partly served (doctor is self-dev-only, H-09). Multi-project identity is not realized in code (H-06).

The FD-002 Class A/B/C consequence-routing model is not implemented as named. The repo's 'Class A/B/C' is an unrelated evidence-retention storage taxonomy (H-01), and the actual consequence routing is a different, richer mission_class x ACP-0..ACP-4 x materiality x quorum matrix (mission-autonomy.yml, risk-materiality.yml, hierarchical-planning.yml). Worse for the 'zero routine prompts' proof: risk-materiality maps ordinary reversible repo mutation to ACP-2 'escalate' with a 2-party quorum and grant-bundle/decision-artifact requirements (H-08), the opposite of Class A/B autonomy. And the canonical authorization is not enforced at an unavoidable launch boundary while a competing executor-built DelegationProof plane persists (H-03). No contract binds the three named FD-002 buckets to autonomous/brokered/stronger-controls routing.

Present: verified no-PR publication + PR escalation route model (default-work-unit.yml route_selection_order with branch-no-pr/direct-main/branch-pr and solo_route_selection preferring the fastest safe route), a Mission Queue + Decision Request CLI, an Adopt/Compatibility path, and a Studio UI. Missing/partial: NO local credentialed broker as a runtime component (H-02, only a policy-grant shell script) — this is the central missing anchor; NO cross-project 'CLI mission inbox' (only per-mission queue + decide list, H-05); multi-project identity not realized in code (H-06); operator-mode setup/diagnose doctor absent (H-09); the vertical's safety property is not enforced at an unavoidable boundary (H-03). The complete-path claim is undermined by the absent broker.

strengths_to_preserve: Single canonical CLI binary `octon` (kernel) with clap subcommands — the right shape for a solo operator; the mission/decide/publish/run verbs are coherent primitives. (.octon/framework/engine/runtime/crates/kernel/src/main.rs:36)

NO distributed-systems breadth in the runtime: grep for raft/consensus/kubernetes/k8s/cluster/multi-node/multi-tenant across framework+instance+crates (excluding target) returned zero subsystem hits — the runtime is genuinely single-host, aligned with FD-001/FD-008.

Mission Queue + Action Slice + Continuation Decision + Autonomy Window primitives and the Decision Request list/resolve CLI are a strong basis for the FD-024 mission inbox — reuse them rather than build new. (.octon/framework/engine/runtime/crates/kernel/src/commands/mission.rs)

Publication route contract already encodes verified no-PR landing, PR escalation, fail-closed conditions, and a solo_route_selection rule preferring the fastest safe route — directly serves FD-024/FD-010. (.octon/framework/product/contracts/default-work-unit.yml:294-320)

Rich, honest autonomy safety machinery: proceed_on_silence with forbidden_action_classes, recovery_windows, autonomy_burn states, circuit_breakers, and safing_defaults — load-bearing reliability primitives worth keeping even if the ACP matrix is simplified. (.octon/instance/governance/policies/mission-autonomy.yml:90-167)

Independent verify path verify_authorized_effect exists in authority_engine as a single canonical function — the right primitive to wire into launch mediation (H-03 fix) rather than reinventing. (.octon/framework/engine/runtime/crates/authority_engine/src/implementation/effects.rs:210)
`octon adopt` (external project adoption preflight) and Compatibility classification give a safe on-ramp for multiple projects. (.octon/framework/engine/runtime/crates/kernel/src/main.rs:80-87)
uncertainties: Whether the ACP-2 'escalate' route + 2-party quorum for ordinary repo mutation actually fires as a human prompt for a solo operator, or is auto-satisfied by mode_defaults (maintenance='notify', reconcile='proceed_on_silence') + an independent verifier acting as the second quorum member. I read the contracts statically but did not execute a run, so the real prompt frequency is UNVERIFIED (feeds H-08).

Whether 'multiple projects' is intended as one .octon install per repo (many roots) or one operator workspace indexing several projects. The code shows a singular per-root project-profile.yml; the multi-project topology is not stated in the crates I read (feeds H-06). REQUIRES_DYNAMIC_PROOF or a design doc to resolve.

Whether the Trust-domain/Federation/Trust-Compact subsystem is dead-on-arrival for the solo path or is load-bearing for provider-native delegation (FD-023). I confirmed the CLI surface and LOC but did not trace whether any solo dogfood workflow depends on it. Recommend confirming with the operator which trust verbs are load-bearing.

Whether a broker is intended to be an in-kernel role rather than a separate process. I searched crate sources for broker/credential-holder and found none, but the intended realization (process vs role) is a design choice not evidenced in source (feeds H-02).

I did not read sibling reviews under .octon/inputs/exploratory/reviews/ (excluded by instruction) and did not run cargo build/test, so all launch-mediation and prompt-frequency claims are STATICALLY_INSPECTED / ARCHITECTURAL_INFERENCE, not DYNAMICALLY_EXECUTED.

Subsystems that look over-built for one operator (simplification candidates, each to be validated against a named safety property before cutting): (1) Federation ledger + Trust Compacts + Trust-domain registry (multi-party); (2) the 7x5 mission_class x ACP-tier matrix where three named FD-002 buckets may suffice; (3) the certification/closure CI cluster (uec-cutover-certify/validate, unified-execution-constitution-closure, closure-certification, closure-validator-sufficiency, assurance-weight-gates, principles-charter-overrides-audit) — heavy gate ceremony; (4) Studio desktop UI (~3.5k LOC) as an additional moving part beyond the CLI; (5) Delegated-authority Leases + portable Proof-bundle import/export if no solo workflow consumes them.

findings.claim: The primary agent-execution engine (lifecycle_executor) launches the candidate agent (codex/claude) WITHOUT ever passing through authority_engine::authorize_execution or verify_authorized_effect. lifecycle_executor has ZERO dependency on authority_engine (no octon_authority_engine in its Cargo.toml, no authority_engine:: usage in src). Its only pre-dispatch gate is its OWN authorize_before_dispatch, which self-constructs and writes a DelegationProof from request.policy.invocation_authority rather than consuming any kernel-issued grant or ExecutorLaunch effect token. Thus the most consequential agent-facing effect path is not completely mediated by the kernel authority.
findings.consequence: Complete mediation (FD tied to single unavoidable authority boundary) does not hold for the agent implementation path. The lifecycle executor is a second, self-attesting authorization plane: it decides its own authority from route.delegation_contract + policy.invocation_authority and dispatches the agent, which then performs arbitrary repo/git/network effects with no kernel grant, no ExecutorLaunch effect-token consumption, and no verify_authorized_effect. issue_executor_launch_effect is called in production ONLY for the studio app launch (commands/mod.rs:736), never for the candidate agent.
findings.minimum_repair: Make lifecycle_executor depend on authority_engine and require a real authorize_execution grant + issue/verify of an ExecutorLaunch effect token immediately before build_executor_command spawns codex/claude; fail closed if the grant/effect is absent. Remove or subordinate the self-built DelegationProof so it can only annotate, never authorize.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a test that invokes the lifecycle_executor adapter for run-packet-implementation with a request whose authority_engine grant is missing/denied and assert the agent process is never spawned (build_executor_command not reached) and the result status is authorization-proof-failed; grep-assert that codex.rs spawn is preceded by a verify_authorized_effect::<ExecutorLaunch> call.

findings.claim: The candidate/agent child process inherits the full ambient parent environment, including any durable credentials (GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC/OPENAI API keys, git credential helpers). No env_clear or env_remove or allowlist is applied at ANY spawn site in the runtime crates.
findings.consequence: Credential separation between the trusted runtime and the untrusted candidate agent does not exist. A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent can read and use any credential present in the runtime's environment to perform authenticated network publication (git push over HTTPS credential helper, gh api merges) entirely outside the authorization boundary. Combined with J-01 this means autonomous durable publication with ambient credentials is reachable from inside the ungated agent spawn.
findings.minimum_repair: Before Command::spawn in build_executor_command, call command.env_clear() then re-inject only an explicit allowlist of non-credential vars (PATH, HOME-for-tool-state, TERM, and any per-run tokens minted by the authority engine). Route all provider/network credential use through a runtime-mediated broker rather than passing ambient env to the child.
findings.acceptance_test: Unit test build_executor_command and assert the resulting Command's env map does not contain GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY when they are set in the parent process (requires env_clear + allowlist to pass).

findings.claim: Exact-SHA publication safety and direct-main autonomous publication: The publication contract lists direct-main at precedence 20 in route_selection_order (before branch-no-pr) and explicitly permits autonomous origin push during closeout. Exact-SHA validation is expressed only as evidence/validator requirements ('route_neutral_exact_sha_check_evidence_when_hosted_publication_claimed') enforced by repo-resident shell scripts, not by a runtime gate at the push site. The runtime does not itself execute git push for this path; the push is performed inside the candidate agent process, and the exact-sha validators live in candidate-editable governance scope.
findings.consequence: Exact-SHA publication safety is not enforced by an unavoidable runtime boundary. Direct-main autonomous publication remains reachable and is route-preferred for solo low-risk changes. The only exact-sha enforcement is post-hoc evidence checked by shell validators under .octon/framework/assurance/.../scripts, which are within the write scope an implementation run can be granted, enabling same-run subversion of the check that governs its own publication. The workflow.rs 'push' reference at line 5440 is only a forbidden-action label in a closeout receipt, not a gated push.
findings.minimum_repair: Perform any origin push / hosted landing only through a gated kernel command (like protected-ci) that (a) computes the expected head SHA in trusted Rust, (b) refuses to publish if the resolved SHA differs, and (c) forbids the publishing run from having write scope over the exact-sha validator scripts. Do not delegate the push to the candidate agent process.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a kernel test asserting that a publication request whose resolved origin head SHA differs from the authorized landed_commit is rejected in Rust before any gh/git push subprocess runs; assert direct-main publication cannot proceed when the implementation run's declared write scope intersects the exact-sha validator script paths.

findings.claim: Effect-token single-use consumption is a non-transactional read-check-then-write with no atomic reservation, no cross-process lock, and non-atomic file persistence (plain fs::write, no temp+rename, no O_EXCL, no fsync). The 'already consumed' guard is checked at effects.rs:564 but status is only flipped and persisted at effects.rs:658 via persist_token_record -> write_json (policy.rs:81-88 plain fs::write). The material effect the token authorizes happens in the caller after verify_authorized_effect returns.
findings.consequence: Idempotency/replay safety is not guaranteed for effect-token single-use. A crash after the material durable effect but before persist_token_record leaves status != consumed, so a crash-retry re-verifies and re-authorizes the same effect -> duplicated durable effect. Two concurrent verifiers can both pass the consumed-check at 564 before either persists at 658 (TOCTOU), double-consuming a single-use token. There is no transactional reserve-then-commit and no exactly-once boundary.
findings.minimum_repair: Reserve atomically before the material effect: create a per-token reservation via OpenOptions::new().create_new(true) (O_EXCL) or an advisory flock held across verify+consume, mark consumed BEFORE returning the VerifiedEffect (reserve-first), and persist records via write-to-temp + atomic rename + fsync. Treat an existing reservation as EFFECT_TOKEN_ALREADY_CONSUMED.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a concurrency test spawning two threads that call verify_authorized_effect on the same single-use token record simultaneously and assert exactly one succeeds; add a crash-simulation test that reserves, injects a failure before persist, retries, and asserts the second attempt is rejected as already-consumed.

findings.claim: Bounded/honest evidence: verify_authorized_effect proves only local internal consistency of a runtime-issued token (allow decision, id/kind/digest match, referenced authority files exist, single-use status), not that the durable effect actually occurred at any provider, nor cryptographic non-repudiation. side_effects/mod.rs INVENTORY is a static DECLARED list of which classes 'should' require the boundary (marked #![allow(dead_code)]) and does not itself enforce mediation. Any language describing this stack as complete-mediation / tamper-proof / attested for provider effects overstates what hash-chained local files prove.
findings.consequence: Claims of tamper-proof / non-repudiation / attestation / complete mediation are only true within the closed world of runtime-written local files and only for effect paths that actually route through the kernel (which the lifecycle_executor agent path does not, per J-01). The evidence is local, mutable by any process with filesystem write (the agent inherits repo write), and not externally verifiable, so it is bounded local audit evidence, not a security proof against a misbehaving candidate.
findings.minimum_repair: Downgrade documentation claims to 'bounded local evidence for kernel-mediated effects only'; enumerate explicitly which effect classes are mediated in code vs declared-only; make side_effects INVENTORY enforced (assert at runtime that every material class in the inventory is reached only via a verified effect) rather than dead_code.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a test that walks the side_effects INVENTORY and, for each material=true entry, asserts a corresponding code path exists that calls verify_authorized_effect before the subprocess; assert the ExecutorLaunch inventory entry maps to a verified launch for the agent executor (currently fails).

findings.claim: Trust admission approval is presence-only, not validated: trust_domain_add sets approved = args.approval_ref.is_some() (trust.rs:302) and flips status from 'blocked' to 'stage_only' purely on the presence of an --approval-ref string, without verifying the referenced approval artifact exists, is well-formed, or is authoritative. (Distinct from protected_ci_auto_merge at mod.rs:1432-1452 which does file-existence-check its projection.)
findings.consequence: Safe trust activation is weak at admission: a candidate can advance a trust domain from blocked to stage_only by passing any arbitrary approval-ref token, without a verified human approval artifact. The cap is stage_only (not execution), and domain_authorizes_execution stays false, so this alone does not authorize effects, but it erodes the intended human boundary and lets self-supplied references stand in for approvals.
findings.minimum_repair: In trust_domain_add, resolve args.approval_ref against the repo, require the artifact to exist, parse it as a valid human-approval envelope, and validate its schema/subject before treating the domain as approved (mirror the file-existence + schema checks already used in protected_ci_auto_merge).
findings.acceptance_test: Add a test calling trust domain add with --approval-ref pointing to a nonexistent or malformed path and assert the resulting domain status is 'blocked' (not 'stage_only').

findings.claim: A second, credentialed control plane exists in GitHub Actions: pr-auto-merge.yml runs on a schedule (cron every 2h) and pull_request_target with contents:write + pull-requests:write and secrets.AUTONOMY_PAT, and decides merge eligibility via repo-resident, PR-head-checked-out shell scripts (evaluate-pr-autonomy-policy.sh and assert_automerge_eligible) before invoking the gated 'octon protected-ci auto-merge'. Because eligibility scripts are checked out from the PR head (git checkout --detach ${head_sha}) and chmod+x'd from that tree, a PR that edits those scripts or the standards JSON can influence its own eligibility gate.
findings.consequence: The autonomous-merge authority and its trigger cadence + credential (AUTONOMY_PAT) live in GitHub Actions, an authority source outside the Rust kernel. While the terminal merge routes through the gated Rust command, the eligibility decision is a candidate-influenceable CI-layer control plane (same-change self-certification risk when a PR mutates its own policy scripts/standards, and pull_request_target grants secrets to code triggered by external PRs). The Rust boundary does not re-derive eligibility from trusted state independent of the PR head.
findings.minimum_repair: Pin eligibility scripts and standards JSON to the base ref (not the PR head) when evaluating merge eligibility; move the eligibility policy evaluation into the trusted Rust protected-ci command using base-ref-pinned inputs; restrict AUTONOMY_PAT usage and avoid running PR-head scripts under pull_request_target with write scope.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a CI/integration assertion that the eligibility evaluation reads policy scripts and standards from the merge base (origin/main) rather than the PR head, and that a PR modifying evaluate-pr-autonomy-policy.sh cannot alter its own auto-merge eligibility outcome.

findings.claim: authorize_execution contains an operator-toggle bypass of runtime-route-bundle freshness verification via env var OCTON_ALLOW_STALE_RUNTIME_ROUTE_BUNDLE, which substitutes verify_runtime_route_bundle with runtime_route_bundle_publication_bypass.
findings.consequence: Even on the properly-gated kernel path, an ambient environment variable weakens a freshness precondition of authorization (route-bundle staleness verification), so an operator or a process controlling the runtime env can dispatch against a stale/bypassed route bundle. This is an env-driven softening of the authorization gate, not a fail-closed boundary.
findings.minimum_repair: Require the stale-bundle bypass to be justified by a signed, human-approved, run-scoped exception artifact rather than a bare environment variable; record and fail-closed if the bypass is used without such an artifact.
findings.acceptance_test: Add a test asserting that setting OCTON_ALLOW_STALE_RUNTIME_ROUTE_BUNDLE=1 without an accompanying approved exception artifact causes authorize_execution to deny rather than proceed via the bypass branch.

decision_alignment.rationale: Complete mediation holds for the kernel command/workflow/pipeline paths (all spawn sites there are preceded by authorize_execution + verify_authorized_effect, e.g. commands/mod.rs:610/725/846/968/1171/1517, workflow.rs:794/952/7156/7522). It does NOT hold for the lifecycle_executor agent-implementation path, which is the primary proposal-execution engine and has zero authority_engine dependency (J-01). Therefore there is no single unavoidable authority boundary for the most consequential agent effects.

The lifecycle_executor self-attests authorization via its own authorize_before_dispatch/DelegationProof built from request.policy.invocation_authority, and GitHub Actions (pr-auto-merge.yml, cron + PAT) is an independent credentialed control/authority plane whose eligibility logic is candidate-influenceable. Both are second control planes competing with authority_engine (J-01, J-07).

No credential separation exists: there is no env_clear/env_remove/allowlist at any runtime spawn site, so candidate agents inherit ambient durable credentials (J-02). The property is simply not implemented.

Effect-token issuance/verification is a real, well-structured gate for kernel-issued effects and studio launch, but the agent executor launch (the effect that lets an untrusted candidate act) is neither issued nor verified as an ExecutorLaunch effect on the lifecycle_executor path, and the child inherits credentials (J-01, J-02).

Route selection and publication are governed by contract prose and shell validators; direct-main autonomous publication is route-preferred and reachable, exact-sha is post-hoc evidence not a runtime push gate, and a stale-route-bundle env bypass softens the authorization precondition (J-03, J-08).

Publication-safety and idempotency intent is present in contract and token design, but exact-sha is not runtime-enforced at the push (J-03), single-use consumption is non-transactional/TOCTOU-prone (J-04), and freshness has an env bypass (J-08).

The gated protected-ci merge command requires a granted approval projection and verified effects (mod.rs:1432-1452,1517-1573), but publication eligibility upstream is decided by PR-head-checked-out shell scripts in GitHub Actions and direct-main push is delegated to the agent, so hosted publication safety is not fully anchored to a trusted, self-cert-resistant gate (J-03, J-07).

Evidence is hash-chained and internally consistent for kernel-mediated effects, but it is local, agent-writable, and does not cover the ungated agent path; single-use consumption lacks a transactional reserve, so evidence can overstate exactly-once and complete-mediation guarantees (J-04, J-05).

The candidate/agent boundary is not enforced: the agent is launched without a kernel grant (J-01) and with full ambient credentials (J-02), and pull_request_target grants secrets to PR-triggered code (J-07). The intended trusted/untrusted separation is breached at the primary execution path.

Human-boundary/trust primitives exist (validate_contract HumanBoundaryRequired, human_only_boundaries, protected-ci approval projection), but trust admission approval is presence-only (J-06) and the human boundary can be bypassed by the self-attesting lifecycle_executor path (J-01) and candidate-influenceable CI eligibility (J-07).

strengths_to_preserve: authority_engine::verify_authorized_effect (effects.rs:210) is a genuinely well-structured token/digest verifier: it checks decision==Allow, kind/request/grant/run id match, canonical record digest match, authority-ref existence, budget, egress, and single-use status, and emits a request+consumed journal pair. Worth keeping and extending to the agent-launch path.

The kernel command/workflow/pipeline paths consistently pair authorize_execution with verify_authorized_effect before every subprocess (commands/mod.rs, workflow.rs, pipeline.rs), demonstrating the intended pattern is implementable and already applied where the kernel owns the effect.

protected_ci_auto_merge (commands/mod.rs:1413-1573) is a good model: it file-existence-checks the approval projection, requires approval_granted, binds an ExecutionRequest with explicit high-risk capabilities, and verifies effects before the gh merge.

lifecycle_executor authorization.rs already fails closed on many governance preconditions (validate_contract, validate_evidence_gates, validate_context_binding, validate_required_receipts, HumanBoundaryRequired for non-safe/new-governance routes) and constrains promotion targets against path escape (authorized_promotion_targets:592-607). These checks are valuable; they just need to be subordinated to a real kernel grant.

side_effects/mod.rs INVENTORY (material-side-effect-inventory) already enumerates the classes that require the authorization boundary including ExecutorLaunch; turning this declared inventory into an enforced invariant is a low-cost path to closing the mediation gap.
The effect-token event journal (effect-token-consumption-requested + effect-token-consumed) provides a good audit spine to build a transactional reserve-then-commit on top of.
uncertainties: I did not execute any code (READ-ONLY, no cargo build/test). The TOCTOU/crash-retry duplication (J-04) and env inheritance (J-02) are inferred from static reading of the spawn/consume code; a dynamic test would upgrade these from STATICALLY_INSPECTED to DYNAMICALLY_EXECUTED/ADVERSARIALLY_TESTED. UNVERIFIED whether an OS-level or wrapper-level sandbox (outside the Rust crates) strips credentials before the runtime process starts.

Whether codex/claude executors apply their own internal sandboxing (the codex command passes --sandbox workspace-write) that might constrain some effects; I did not inspect the external codex/claude binaries, so the net exploitability of J-02 (credential use for network publication) from inside the agent is ARCHITECTURAL_INFERENCE, not proven.

I inspected the two most authority-relevant GitHub workflows (pr-auto-merge.yml, main-push-safety.yml) and the merge script; I did not exhaustively read all 42 workflows, so there may be additional CI-layer authority surfaces beyond J-07.

protected-ci-auto-merge.sh delegates to run_octon_kernel; I confirmed the terminal merge is gated in Rust, but I did not trace run_octon_kernel's resolution to confirm it always resolves to the built, unpatched binary rather than a repo-editable wrapper.

The intake handoff unit at .octon/inputs/additive/.incoming/... was treated as research-only per instructions and NOT relied upon; some FD target wording is inferred from the assignment summary rather than a canonical decisions file I read directly, so FD numbering-to-property mapping carries residual ambiguity.

I did not verify whether git push over HTTPS actually has a credential helper configured in the target deployment environment; J-02's network-publication consequence assumes ambient git/gh credentials are present, which is DEPLOYMENT_LOCAL and unverified here.
